request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital, coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You answer in exactly the format requested and add nothing else.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient: XXXXXXX

Date of Admission: XXXXXXX

Date of Discharge: XXXXXXX
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:

Upon admission, the patient presented with acute onset epigastric pain associated with vomiting. Subsequently, she was diagnosed with acute pancreatitis and a dilated common bile duct with no gallstones or other pathology. Further, a MRCP revealed a curious cystic lesion lying posterior to the head of the pancreas causing extrinsic compression. An abdominal CT scan revealed a cystic or necrotic mass behind the head of the pancreas representing an inflammatory lesion or abscess.

During admission, the patient was treated with oral antibiotics and observed clinically and haematologically. However, her bilirubin continued to rise. An ERCP revealed a 10 cm duodenal diverticular abscess at the level of the major papilla draining pus and bile, likely causing extrinsic compression of the bile duct.

The patient experienced clinical and hematological improvement and was discharged with a plan for follow-up with the gastroenterology team.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Instructions:

The patient is advised to follow-up with the gastroenterology team and adhere to any prescribed medications. Additionally, the patient is instructed to consume a healthy diet and maintain a low-risk lifestyle.

Follow-Up Care:

Follow-up with the gastroenterology team.

Signed:

XXXXXXXXX

Answer with one line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The admission was for acute pancreatitis, but investigation found a duodenal diverticular abscess compressing the bile duct. Acute pancreatitis was the presenting diagnosis. Whether it was actually the cause is unclear, since the abscess may have caused the extrinsic compression and the rising bilirubin.

The options are:
- K57: diverticular disease of the intestine. K57.0 and K57.2 cover perforation and abscess, but K57 is for the large and small intestine, and duodenum is included in the small intestine. A duodenal diverticulum with abscess would be K57.0 or K57.1, or K57.8 with abscess.
- K85: acute pancreatitis, which was diagnosed during the stay.
- K22.5: diverticulum of the oesophagus, which is not relevant.
- K31.7: polyp of the stomach and duodenum, which is not relevant.

The ERCP finding of a 10 cm duodenal diverticular abscess draining pus and bile was established after investigation and is the likely cause of the pancreatitis picture, the bile duct compression and the rising bilirubin. The condition chiefly responsible for the episode is therefore the duodenal diverticulitis with abscess, which falls in K57.

CODE: K57
